forehand.label: Topspin forehand
forehand.summary: The modern forehand: unit turn, load the outside leg, drop the racket below the ball and brush up through contact out in front.

phases.name: Ready & split step
phases.caption: Knees bent, weight on the balls of the feet. Split step as the opponent strikes so you can push off in either direction.

phases.name: Unit turn
phases.caption: Hips and shoulders turn together as one unit. The left hand stays on the racket then points at the ball. Weight loads onto the right (back) leg.

phases.name: Load & racket drop
phases.caption: The racket head drops below the ball, butt cap pointing at it. The back leg is firm and bent: this is the spring. Hips begin to rotate before the arm moves.

phases.name: Contact
phases.caption: Legs drive up, hips fire, the arm lags then whips through. Contact is in front of the body at hip-to-chest height with the racket brushing low-to-high.

phases.name: Finish & recover
phases.caption: Finish over the opposite shoulder (or windscreen-wiper across the body on high balls). Weight has moved onto the front foot; recover with a crossover step.

mistakes: Arm-only swing with no shoulder turn
Contact late (beside the body) instead of in front
Standing tall: no knee bend means no leg drive

backhand_2h.label: Two-handed backhand
backhand_2h.summary: The most stable stroke in the game: both hands turn the racket back with the shoulders, the hips drive, and the top hand pushes through contact.

phases.name: Ready & split step
phases.caption: Same ready position as the forehand. Both hands on the grip, racket in front.

phases.name: Unit turn
phases.caption: Turn the shoulders fully; the racket goes back because the shoulders turn, not because the arms pull. The back (left) leg takes the weight.

phases.name: Load & drop
phases.caption: Knees bend, racket head drops below the ball. Keep the hands away from the body so the swing has room.

phases.name: Contact
phases.caption: Hips open first, then shoulders. Both arms extend through the ball in front of the body at waist-to-chest height. The top hand drives the racket.

phases.name: Finish
phases.caption: Finish high over the right shoulder with the chest facing the net. Weight is on the front foot.

mistakes: Bottom hand dominates (hits like a weak forehand)
Hands too close to the body
Opening the shoulders early

backhand_1h.label: One-handed backhand
backhand_1h.summary: Elegant and demanding: a full shoulder coil, a step across, contact well in front with a straight arm, and the free arm thrown back for balance.

phases.name: Ready & split step
phases.caption: Ready position; the left hand cradles the throat so it can help take the racket back.

phases.name: Unit turn & high set
phases.caption: Shoulders turn until the back nearly faces the net. The left hand takes the racket back high. Weight on the back (left) leg.

phases.name: Step across & drop
phases.caption: Step across with the right foot (closed stance), knees bent. The racket drops below the ball as the left hand lets go.

phases.name: Contact
phases.caption: Contact far in front with a straight arm. The shoulders stay sideways; the left arm swings back to counter-balance.

phases.name: Finish
phases.caption: A high finish with the arms spread. Hold the sideways position until the ball is gone, then recover.

mistakes: Opening the shoulders before contact
Bent hitting arm (contact too close)
No step across: hitting off the back foot

slice.label: Backhand slice
slice.summary: High-to-low with a slightly open face, driven THROUGH the ball so it skids low. Buys time, changes rhythm and sets up the forehand.

phases.name: Ready & split step
phases.caption: Ready position, Continental grip already in hand.

phases.name: Turn & set high
phases.caption: Full shoulder turn with the racket set up high, above the ball. The left hand holds the throat.

phases.name: Step across
phases.caption: Step across with the right foot into a closed stance. The racket stays high; the face is slightly open.

phases.name: Contact
phases.caption: High-to-low but mostly forward: drive through the ball, do not chop under it. Contact slightly in front, left arm goes back.

phases.name: Finish
phases.caption: Arms spread like wings; the racket finishes pointing at the target. The ball stays low and skids.

mistakes: Chopping down steeply (ball floats)
Face too open
Not turning the shoulders

serve.label: Serve
serve.summary: Rhythm, toss, trophy, racket drop, explode up and pronate. The only shot you control completely.

phases.name: Stance & rhythm
phases.caption: Side-on to the baseline, front foot angled toward the net post. Ball in the left hand, racket relaxed. Rock gently to start the rhythm.

phases.name: Toss & trophy
phases.caption: Toss with a straight arm to a spot just inside the court. Knees bend, hips push forward, the racket arm forms the trophy with the tip pointing up.

phases.name: Racket drop
phases.caption: As the legs drive up, the racket drops deep behind the back. Elbow high, forearm loose. Deepest knee bend here.

phases.name: Contact
phases.caption: Full extension, body airborne, contact in front and above the head. Forearm pronates so the strings face the target. Left arm tucks into the body.

phases.name: Landing
phases.caption: Land inside the baseline on the left foot, back leg kicks up for balance, racket finishes across the body. Immediately split step.

mistakes: Toss too far behind or to the side
No leg drive (arm-only serve)
Hitting with a forehand grip (no pronation)

return.label: Return of serve
return.summary: Short backswing, early contact, use the server's pace. The goal is a deep, neutral ball and a reset to the middle.

phases.name: Wide ready stance
phases.caption: Wider than a normal ready position, weight forward, eyes on the toss.

phases.name: Split step
phases.caption: Hop as the server hits so you land as the ball crosses the net, ready to push off.

phases.name: Compact turn
phases.caption: Shoulder turn only; the racket barely goes back. The left hand points at the ball.

phases.name: Block contact
phases.caption: Contact in front with a firm wrist. Let the serve supply the pace; aim deep to the middle.

phases.name: Short finish & recover
phases.caption: Abbreviated follow-through. Recover to the middle of the baseline before the next ball.

mistakes: Full backswing against a fast serve
Standing flat-footed (no split step)
Trying to win the point on the return

volley.label: Volley
volley.summary: Short punch, racket head above the wrist, step across into the ball. The feet volley; the arm just presents the strings.

phases.name: Ready at the net
phases.caption: Racket out in front, head up, knees bent, weight forward.

phases.name: Split step
phases.caption: Hop as the opponent strikes. Land light and balanced.

phases.name: Turn & set
phases.caption: Turn the shoulders, not the arm; the racket moves a few inches, no more. Racket head stays above the wrist.

phases.name: Step across & punch
phases.caption: Step across with the opposite foot into the ball and punch forward. Contact in front, firm wrist, face slightly open.

phases.name: Short finish
phases.caption: The follow-through is short; move through the volley toward the net to cover the reply.

mistakes: Swinging at the volley
Racket head drooping below the wrist
Standing still instead of stepping across

dropshot.label: Drop shot
dropshot.summary: Disguise is everything: prepare like a drive, then soften the grip, open the face and cut under the ball at the last instant.

phases.name: Ready & split step
phases.caption: Same as a groundstroke. The opponent should not know what is coming.

phases.name: Disguised unit turn
phases.caption: Identical to the forehand drive: full shoulder turn, weight on the back leg.

phases.name: Late change
phases.caption: At the last moment the grip softens to Continental and the face opens. The racket comes forward high rather than dropping below the ball.

phases.name: Soft contact
phases.caption: A short, downward-forward cut under the ball with soft hands. Think "catch the ball on the strings".

phases.name: Short finish & move in
phases.caption: The racket stops almost immediately. Move forward: a good drop shot is followed by a volley or a pass.

mistakes: Telegraphing with a different preparation
Hitting it from behind the baseline
Too much backspin, not enough touch

overhead.label: Overhead smash
overhead.summary: Turn sideways, point at the ball, shuffle back, then serve it: same mechanics as a serve with footwork added.

phases.name: Turn & point
phases.caption: As soon as the lob goes up, turn sideways and point at the ball with the left hand. Racket up behind the head.

phases.name: Shuffle back
phases.caption: Small sideways shuffle steps, staying under the ball. Keep pointing.

phases.name: Racket drop
phases.caption: Racket drops behind the back, knees bend, back leg loaded.

phases.name: Contact
phases.caption: Explode up, full extension, contact slightly in front. Snap the wrist through the ball.

phases.name: Finish
phases.caption: Racket finishes across the body; land balanced and recover to the net.

mistakes: Backpedalling instead of turning sideways
Letting the ball drop too low
Not pointing at the ball

tweener.label: Tweener (between the legs)
tweener.summary: For a lob you cannot otherwise reach: sprint, let the ball drop below the knees, flick between the legs. Low percentage, high joy.

phases.name: Sprint back
phases.caption: Turn and sprint after the lob with the racket low. Do not look back yet.

phases.name: Track the bounce
phases.caption: Let the ball bounce and run past it so the ball drops between your legs.

phases.name: Straddle
phases.caption: Feet wide, racket pointing straight down behind you, ball at knee height.

phases.name: Flick
phases.caption: A sharp wrist flick through the ball between the legs. Aim high over the net; your opponent is usually at net.

phases.name: Turn & see
phases.caption: Turn immediately to see where it went and get back into the point.

mistakes: Trying it when a normal lob is possible
Hitting before the ball has dropped low enough
Not turning around afterwards
